small_guidance:
- The output spatial size is OH*OW=3844 and OC=16; current grid wastes work when BLOCK_OC>16. Pin BLOCK_OC=16 (since OC=16 exactly) and sweep BLOCK_N in {64,128,256,512} with num_warps in {4,8} and num_stages in {2,3,4}. Drop all BLOCK_OC>16 configs.
- Swap the program axes so pid_oc is axis 0 (size 1 when BLOCK_OC=16) and (N*OD, OH*OW tile) collapse into a single large axis — this improves L2 reuse of the 16×27 weight tile across many spatial tiles. Also try grouping N*OD*tile_hw into one axis with a swizzle for better L2 locality.
- Preload the entire weight tensor (OC*IC*KD*KH*KW = 16*3*27 = 1296 floats ≈ 5KB) once into registers/shared outside the loops using a single `tl.load` with a 2D index, then reuse across all spatial tiles — but since each program only processes one (n,od) tile, instead try caching weight in constant memory by passing it as a small constexpr-shape load, or unroll IC×KD×KH×KW completely (already done via static_range). Verify the compiler is actually hoisting w loads.
large_guidance:
- Restructure to a true im2col GEMM: M=OC (16), N=N*OD*OH*OW (per-batch or whole-batch), K=IC*KD*KH*KW (27). With M=16 and K=27 both tiny, the right shape is a tall-skinny GEMM where each program computes a [16, BLOCK_N] output tile by loading the full 16×27 weight matrix once and streaming input patches. Use BLOCK_N=128 or 256, num_warps=4.
- Consider an output-stationary kernel persistent over N*OD: one program per (n, od) computes all OH*OW outputs for all 16 OC, keeping the 16×27 weight in registers and the bias/scale/bias-vec (16 each) hot. This eliminates redundant weight reloads across the OH*OW tiles entirely.
- Alternatively, switch input layout to NDHWC (channels-last) so the inner-K reduction over IC is contiguous and can be vectorized with `tl.dot` against a [27,16] weight matrix — this lets you use tensor cores via tf32 `tl.dot` for the GEMM portion, currently the kernel is doing scalar FMAs.
